blocks.text: Two SS3 classes both have a mean Mathematics score of 60. In one class almost everyone scored between 55 and 65. In the other, scores run from 20 to 95. The mean hides that difference. A measure of dispersion — range, IQR, mean deviation or standard deviation — is what tells you how spread out the scores really are.

blocks.markdown:
The **range** is $\text{largest} - \text{smallest}$. It is quick, but one extreme value (a ₦20 loaf among ₦3 loaves) inflates it.

The **interquartile range** uses the middle half of the data:

$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.

For an ordered list, $Q_1$ is the median of the lower half and $Q_3$ is the median of the upper half (leave out the overall median when $n$ is odd). For an ogive, read $Q_1$ at $\frac{n}{4}$ and $Q_3$ at $\frac{3n}{4}$.

blocks.title: Mean deviation, variance and standard deviation
blocks.text: Mean deviation $= \frac{\sum |x - \bar{x}|}{n}$. Variance (WAEC) is $\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum (x - \bar{x})^2}{n}$. Standard deviation is $\sigma = \sqrt{\sigma^2}$. WAEC divides by $n$, not by $n-1$, unless the question specifically asks for the sample formula.

items: Subtract the mean from each value to get the deviations $x - \bar{x}$.
For mean deviation, take absolute values, add, and divide by $n$.
For variance, square the deviations, add, and divide by $n$.
For standard deviation, take the square root of the variance.

blocks.title: Mean deviation and variance
blocks.prompt: For the data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, find the mean deviation and the variance (divide by n).

steps.text: Mean deviation is the average of those.
Variance divides that sum by n, not n − 1.

blocks.markdown:
### Comparing two data sets

When two sets have the **same mean**, the one with the smaller range, IQR or standard deviation is more **consistent** — its values cluster more tightly around that mean.

If the means are different, you can still compare spread, but you must say so clearly: a standard deviation of ₦$20$ around a mean of ₦$400$ is tighter than a standard deviation of ₦$60$ around the same mean. Never treat a larger $\sigma$ as "better" — in most school contexts, smaller spread is more consistent.

blocks.title: WAEC tip on $n$ versus $n-1$
blocks.text: Unless a question says "sample standard deviation" or "divide by $n-1$", use $\sigma^2 = \sum (x-\bar{x})^2 / n$. The $n-1$ formula is for sample statistics in some later courses and is a very popular wrong option. Also: mean deviation uses $|x-\bar{x}|$; dropping the absolute-value signs makes the deviations cancel and the answer collapse to $0$.

points: WAEC variance is $\sigma^2 = \sum (x - \bar{x})^2 / n$; standard deviation is its square root.
Do not divide by $n-1$ unless the question says so.
Of two sets with the same mean, the smaller standard deviation (or IQR) is the more consistent set.
